## In a nutshell - Border agreement in force from 1 January 2024 - Withholding tax withheld only in Switzerland - Excess €10,000 for new frontier workers - Switzerland not an EU/EEA member
## Key facts - **What**: New Italy-Switzerland Border Agreement - When: Signed December 23, 2020, effective January 1, 2024 - Where: Swiss Confederation and Italian Republic - Who: G border workers working in Switzerland and residing in Italy - Amount: Deductible €10,000 for new frontier workers, exemption €7,500 for old frontier workers
The border agreement signed on 23 December 2020 entered into force on 1 January 2024, replacing the previous regime after Italian ratification with Law 83 of 13 June 2023. This agreement establishes that the tax at source on employee income is withheld exclusively in Switzerland, while Italy avoids double taxation through the tax credit to be declared in the EC framework of form 730. Switzerland confirms its position of not belonging to the European Union or the European Economic Area (EEA), as provided for in the Double Taxation Convention signed on 9 December 1976.
For frontier workers, the agreement introduces important distinctions: those who were already frontier workers before 17 July 2023 benefit from a transitional regime valid until 2033 with an exemption of €7,500, while new frontier workers (those who started their activity after that date) have ## Practical analysis of the cost of living in St. Gallen in the national context
Living and working as a cross-border commuter in Switzerland involves a direct comparison between the costs incurred beyond the Alps and the purchasing power in Italy, which is particularly relevant for those who live in the province of St. Gallen. Although the source does not provide specific data on rents or consumer prices in the canton of St. Gallen, it is possible to analyze the tax and contribution implications that directly affect disposable income.
The €10,000 exemption for new cross-border commuters is a key element: this amount is deducted from the Swiss gross income before withholding tax is applied, reducing the tax base. For example, an employee with a gross annual income of CHF 60,000 would only see tax levied on CHF 50,000 after the deductible, resulting in tax savings compared to a full rate. This mechanism is particularly advantageous in cantons with low municipal rates, as may be the case in some San Welsh areas.
However, compulsory contributions in Switzerland have an impact on the net: in addition to withholding tax, 5.3% for AHV/IV/EO, 1.1% for ALV/AC (up to the ceiling), the variable UVG premium and the BVG contribution must be considered. These deductions, although intended for forms of social security, reduce the net salary received monthly. In Italy, on the other hand, the tax credit recognized allows you to offset all or part of the Swiss tax paid, avoiding double taxation through the declaration in the EC framework of 730.
At the national level, the fact that Switzerland is not part of the EU/EEA has practical consequences: cross-border commuters do not benefit from the free movement of services in the same way as EU/EEA citizens, although the bilateral agreement specifically regulates their situation. Bodies such as SECO monitor the economic impact of these agreements, while the USTAT and the BFS collect statistical data on employment and cross-border commuters for intercantonal comparisons.
For those considering a move or a new job as a cross-border commuter, it is essential to consider not only the gross salary offered, but also the combined effect of deductible, withholding tax rates (which vary from canton to canton), social contributions and real purchasing power in Italy, taking into account exchange rates and cross-border inflation.

Per gestire correttamente la propria posizione fiscale e previdenziale come frontaliero in Svizzera, è necessario seguire alcuni passaggi concreti basati sulle disposizioni dell'accordo in vigore dal 1 gennaio 2024. Prima di tutto, verificare la propria categoria: se si è iniziato a lavorare in Svizzera dopo il 17 luglio 2023, si rientra nella categoria dei 'nuovi frontalieri' con diritto alla franchigia di €10'000; se invece si era già attivi prima di quella data, si applica il regime transitorio con esenzione di €7'500 valido fino al 2033. Questa distinzione va comunicata tempestivamente al datore di lavoro svizzero affinché possa applicare correttamente la trattenuta alla fonte.
In Svizzera, l'imposta alla fonte viene calcolata e trattenuta direttamente dal datore di lavoro, che la riversa all'Amministrazione Federale delle Contribuzioni (AFC/ESTV) tramite le autorità cantonali delle contribuzioni. Non è necessario presentare una dichiarazione annuale in Svizzera unless si hanno altri redditi oltre quello da lavoro dipendente. Tuttavia, è fondamentale conservare il certificato di stipendio annuale, che riporta l'imposta alla fonte effettivamente trattenuta.
In Italia, entro i termini ordinari di presentazione del modello 730 (solitamente tra aprile e giugno dell'anno successivo), bisogna dichiarare il reddito prodotto in Svizzera nel quadro CE, indicando l'imposta alla fonte già versata. L'Agenzia delle Entrate riconosce poi un credito d'imposta pari all'imposta svizzera pagata, evitando così la doppia imposizione. È consigliabile rivolgersi a un CAF o a un professionista abilitato per la compilazione, soprattutto se si hanno detrazioni familiari o altri redditi da dichiarare.
Per quanto riguarda la previdenza, i contributi AVS/AI/IPG versati in Svizzera contribuiscono al diritto alle prestazioni svizzere di vecchiaia, invalidità e perdita di guadagno. Anche se si risiede in Italia, è possibile richiedere il totale o parziale trasferimento dei contributi verso l'INPS mediante le convenzioni internazionali, oppure mantenere la contribuzione nel sistema svizzero per futura pensione. Lo stesso vale per la LPP/BVG: i versamenti possono essere trasferiti o lasciati nel fondo pensione occupazionale, a seconda delle norme del proprio piano pensionistico.
Infine, per l'assicurazione malattia, i frontalieri G hanno diritto d'opzione tra la Lamal svizzera e l'assistenza italiana, da esercitare entro tre mesi dall'inizio dell'attività. La scelta è irrevocabile salvo cambiamenti di situazione lavorativa o di residenza. item.title: One Year After Tariff Shock, Exporters Still Uncertain
item.description: One year after the 39% US duties, the rate on Swiss goods is 12.5% but remains unpredictable: negotiations, rulings and new investigations keep exporters on their toes
item.content:encoded:
## In a nutshell - On April 2, 2025 Trump announced tariffs of 10% base plus reciprocal - Switzerland initially planned a duty of 31%, then increased to 39% - After negotiations and judgments, the rate currently in force is 12.5% - A maximum ceiling of 15% was agreed in the November 2025 Memorandum of Understanding
## Key facts - **What**: US duties on Swiss exports - When: Initial announcement on 2 April 2025, scheduled to take effect on 7 August 2025 - Where: Zurich, home to the main exporters' associations - Who: US Government under Trump, Swiss Federal Council - Amount: Current rate of 12.5%, initially planned at 31%, then increased to 39%, agreed ceiling of 15%
A year ago, the stranglehold of US tariffs hit the Swiss export economy with all its might. The punitive tariffs of 39% announced at the time had sparked fears of a collapse in exports, falling margins and thousands of jobs at risk. 12 months later, exporters still have to contend with a rate of 12.5%.
The 39% rate represented the temporary highlight of a development that had already begun several months earlier. On 2 April 2025, US President Donald Trump had announced, on his so-called “Liberation Day”, a 10% basic duty on almost all imports, in addition to additional country-specific “reciprocal” duties.
For ## Analysis of implications for Swiss exports
The persistence of a US customs rate of 12.5% on Swiss goods represents a significant additional cost for exporting companies, particularly in traditionally strong sectors such as precision mechanics, watchmaking and the pharmaceutical chemical industry. This burden adds to the already high pressures on the cost of living in Switzerland, indirectly influencing pricing strategies and international competitiveness.
From a business perspective, the unpredictability described in the source creates difficulties in medium- and long-term planning. While the current rate of 12.5% is lower than both the peak of 39% and the agreed ceiling of 15%, the possibility of a new tightening linked to the industrial overcapacity survey keeps the level of attention high. This scenario is particularly relevant considering that exports constitute a significant share of Swiss GDP, with direct impacts on employment in industrial cantons such as Zurich, Bern and Basel.
The shift from legal foundations such as IEEPA to those based on Section 301 of the Trade Act regarding forced labor demonstrates how US trade policy can move quickly between different legal justifications. For Swiss companies, this requires constant monitoring not only of the effective rates, but also of the underlying motivations

In fronte alla persistente incertezza sulla politica commerciale statunitense, le imprese esportatrici svizzere possono adottare diverse misure concrete per mitigare i rischi e mantenere la competitività.
1) Monitoraggio attivo delle fonti ufficiali: seguire regolarmente gli aggiornamenti del SECO (Stato Segretariato dell'Economia) sulle politiche commerciali statunitensi e le comunicazioni dell'Ambasciata svizzera a Washington. Il SECO pubblica bollettini settimanali sulle evoluzioni doganali che interessano l'export svizzero.
2) Diversificazione dei mercati: valutare l'espansione verso mercati meno volatili come l'Unione Europea, la Cina o i paesi emergenti dell'Asia sud-orientale. Secondo i dati storici citati nella fonte, la dipendenza dal mercato statunitense ha rappresentato un punto di vulnerabilità durante la crisi dei dazi del 2025.
3) Analisi dell'impatto sui costi: calcolare precisamente l'effetto dell'aliquota del 12,5% sui margini di profitto per linea di prodotto. Questa analisi dovrebbe includere scenari di possibili aumenti fino al tetto concordato del 15%, per preparare piani di contingenza.
4) Coinvolgimento delle associazioni di categoria: partecipare attivamente ai lavori delle associazioni esportatrici svizzere (come Swissmem per la meccanica o chimie.swiss per l'industria chimica) che mantengono canali di dialogo sia con il Consiglio federale che con le autorità statunitensi.
5) Valutazione di strumenti di copertura: esplorare con la propria banca o consulente finanziario la possibilità di utilizzare strumenti assicurativi o finanziari per coprire il rischio di variazioni improvvise delle tariffe doganali, sebbene la fonte non specifichi quali strumenti siano attualmente disponibili o consigliati.
Per approfondire queste tematiche e accedere a strumenti pratici di supporto alle decisioni esportatorie, invitiamo gli imprenditori a utilizzare il [calcolatore dei costi di esportazione](nav:calculator) disponibile sul nostro sito, che permette di simulare l'impatto di diverse aliquote doganali sui margini di profitto aziendali.

## In brief - It is noted that the heat is not experienced equally by everyone in Geneva - Survey conducted in the summer of 2025 on over 1000 residents - Two thirds regularly suffered from the heat at home - Three out of four people report sleep disturbances
## Key facts - **What**: Report on summer comfort and inequalities - When: Summer 2025 - Where: Geneva - Who: University of Geneva as part of the SWICE project - Amount: Over 1000 Geneva residents surveyed
As heatwaves multiply, the city of Geneva is discovering that the heat is not experienced equally by everyone. A report entitled 'Le confort estival à Genève', recently published by the local university as part of the SWICE project (individual and collective sustainable well-being in the energy transition), reveals that the ability to cope with high temperatures is strongly influenced by citizens' social and housing profiles. The survey, conducted in the summer of 2025 on over 1000 Geneva residents, analyzed the effects of heat on daily life and the strategies implemented to cope with it, reports the Tribune de Genève. The results are clear: the consequences of heatwaves depend not only on the weather, but also on factors such as income, type of housing, state of health, gender, and neighborhood of residence. Nearly two thirds of those surveyed stated that they regularly suffered from the heat in their homes during the summers of 2024 and 2025. Sleep disturbances are the most widespread problem, affecting three out of four people, followed by difficulty concentrating, dehydration, and irritability, with a negative impact on general well-being. A significant finding concerns disparity: women and gender minorities, people with modest incomes, tenants, residents in dense urban areas, the elderly, and those with health problems are much more exposed. Vulnerability to heat is the result of a combination of social, economic, and environmental factors that determine adaptive capacity, and these factors tend to accumulate, states Alice Guilbert, a researcher at the Institute of Environmental Sciences at the University of Geneva, in statements reported by the press. Women, in particular, suffer more from the effects of heat due to a heavier domestic and family burden, which limits flexibility in daily organization and the possibility of modifying their activities during heat peaks. This situation highlights how living conditions and daily responsibilities directly influence the health and well-being of specific segments of the population during periods of severe heatwaves.
